PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT / WORK PRODUCT. PARTIAL MEMO: external-law verification was blocked (egress proxy denied the first fetches); legal propositions below come from counsel's own recollection and are UNVERIFIED against primary text. Document-based findings are verified.

BOTTOM LINE
1. Treat May 2, 2025 as discovery for HIPAA (45 CFR 164.404(a)(2)/164.410 key on when the breach is known or would be known with reasonable diligence, to any workforce member/agent; not on the Privacy Officer's determination). Internal Policy HIPAA-BN-2025-004 (discovery = written determination, May 16) conflicts with the regulation and should not be relied on or defended; amend it. The BAA's own definition (Template s.1.2(b)) is also knowledge-based, so the BAA clock is May 2 regardless.
2. Key dates (May 2 basis): BAA s.4.1 five-business-day successful-incident report May 9 (already passed); BAA s.4.3 client notice June 1, 2025 (a Sunday; send by Fri May 30); CO/FL/WA 30-day individual deadlines June 1; OH/OR/WI 45 days June 16; HIPAA outer limit 60 days July 1. Plan all individual notice by May 30-June 1. May 16 alternatives (June 15 / July 15) are not safe.
3. Encryption safe harbor unavailable: AES-256 at rest, but data left through the API decrypted, plaintext JSON; key not compromised but irrelevant (Forensic Report ss.4.4, 7). Breach of unsecured PHI for all 83,400 (61,200 with SSN).
4. Dual-track premise needs correction: for the 35 telehealth clients, the SaaS Agreement s.2.3 makes the client 'solely responsible for the patient-provider relationship'; Evergreen looks like a business associate operating without a BAA (164.502(e), 164.308(b) violation), not a covered entity. Do not self-designate as CE and notify HHS/individuals/media directly without resolving this; default plan: notify the 35 clients (164.410, SaaS s.8.2 'promptly') and offer to run notice for them. Note internal inconsistency: timeline says 7 telehealth clients among 42 affected clients; email/spreadsheet/forensic report say 35 clients (9,400 individuals). Resolve.
5. If Evergreen is an agent of CE clients, Evergreen's May 2 knowledge may be imputed to each CE (164.404(a)(2)), starting the CEs' 60 days on May 2, not on receipt of Evergreen's notice. Another reason to notify clients now.

DELIVERABLE LEDGER (each item addressed)
A. Federal HIPAA: BA to CE notice 164.410 (without unreasonable delay, <=60 days); CE to individuals 164.404 (first-class mail; content: what happened incl. dates of breach and discovery, PHI types, protective steps, mitigation, contact incl. toll-free number); HHS 164.408 for 500+ contemporaneously; media 164.406 for >500 residents of a State. CORRECTION: the email thread and spreadsheet cite 164.408 for media and 164.406(a) for HHS; the sections are reversed (media=406, HHS=408). Media trigger is per-State residents; all 14 States exceed 500 (smallest Montana 1,500), but media duty falls on the covered entity (each client; Evergreen only if a CE). Substitute notice if 10+ individuals lack contact data (web 90 days or major media, toll-free number). Law-enforcement delay 164.412 not invoked. Burden of proof on notification: 164.414(b).
B. Discovery date: see Bottom Line 1; sources: Forensic Report s.3, s.8 (SOC alert 2:17 AM May 2, escalated to CISO 3:15, IR activated 3:45, endpoint disabled 6:00); Timeline May 2 and May 16 entries; Email Haskell 5/18. Note Haskell's May 18 email concedes May 2 but Timeline (5/16) shows she 'designated' May 16; reconcile in the file.
C. BA vs CE tracks: BA track (312 BAAs; ~74,000 individuals): notify CEs by June 1 with s.4.3(a)-(f) content, in installments allowed; CEs handle individuals/HHS/media. Because BAA s.4.5 bars Evergreen from contacting HHS or regulators about CE PHI without CE written consent (except as required by law), obtain written CE authority before running notices or AG filings for them. Telehealth track (35 clients, ~9,400): see Bottom Line 4; remedy the missing BAAs (164.502(e), 164.504(e)); Risk Assessment Item #9 (Nov 2024, target Q2 2025) shows prior knowledge of the gap, aggravating penalty exposure.
D. State chart (individual deadline / regulator; per client documents, flagged where my recollection differs and needs verification): TX 60 days; AG if 250+, my understanding is AG notice within 30 days (2023 amendment) - spreadsheet omits the 30-day AG limit and 'TX HHS' filing is unsupported. CA expedient; AG sample copy if 500+; CMIA. IL without delay; AG threshold stated as 'any number' in spreadsheet but 500+ in Policy App. B (my recollection: 500+; and HIPAA-compliant entities notify AG within 5 business days of HHS) - conflict unresolved. NY spreadsheet says no fixed days; my recollection is a 30-day cap added Dec 2024 plus DFS notice; spreadsheet lists 'State Police', Policy lists DHSES - conflict unresolved; AG/DOS/State Police/DFS all to be checked. FL 30 days (+15 for good cause), Dept of Legal Affairs 500+; Florida also imposes a short third-party-agent notice to the data owner (my recollection ~10 days: verify). OR 45 days, AG 250+; vendor-to-owner 10 days (verify). LA 60 days; spreadsheet says no AG notice, Policy App. B says AG at 1,000+; my recollection: LAC 16:III.701 requires AG notice within 10 days of resident notice - conflict unresolved. WI 45 days; no AG; PI excludes health data so non-SSN individuals may fall outside the statute. OH 45 days; Policy App. B says AG at 1,000+, spreadsheet says none; my recollection: none. CO 30 days; AG 500+. CT 60 days; AG; SSN triggers identity-theft services (24 months, verify). WA 30 days; AG 500+. MA as soon as practicable; AG + OCABR; letter may not describe nature of breach or number affected; credit monitoring 18 months where SSN (verify). MT without delay; spreadsheet says AG only if substitute notice; my recollection: AG consumer protection copy required simultaneously - conflict, verify. Also check consumer-reporting-agency notice thresholds (commonly 1,000+) in each State, and HIPAA deemed-compliance carve-outs (varying by State). Maintainer/vendor duties to notify data owners 'immediately' (TX, WA, IL, CT) are shorter than the BAA 30 days: confirm whether the May 3 'initial notification' to Lakeshore (Kowalski email) occurred; the Timeline says the May 2 system notice did not mention a security incident and Calloway advised holding client notices on May 3. Resolve this factual conflict immediately; it determines state vendor-duty exposure and BAA s.4.1 compliance.
E. Content: use a base letter with State addenda (agree with Calloway; CA, CT, MA, NY have prescriptive content). 
F. Part 2 (Clearwater, 6,100): Evergreen is likely a qualified service organization to a Part 2 program. The thread says the 2024 Part 2 rule was effective February 16, 2024; my recollection is that it was effective April 16, 2024 with compliance by February 16, 2026 (verify, 89 Fed. Reg. 12472), so the Part 2 breach rule (42 CFR 2.16(b)) may not yet be mandatory; either way HIPAA applies to the PHI, notice goes through HHS OCR, and I know of no separate SAMHSA filing (verify). Use generic descriptor ('health and treatment records') only if it still satisfies 164.404(c)(1)(B) (types of PHI) and State content rules; check NY mental-health confidentiality law and Clearwater's consent. Mailing envelope must not reveal treatment.
G. Pediatric (Pine Ridge, 3,800 minors): notice to parent/guardian as personal representative (164.502(g)); Pine Ridge's offer to supply contacts (Timeline 5/17) vs Haskell's contact request - confirm one channel; 'responsible party' field may be stale; use minor identity monitoring (Sentinel) and FAQ; Wisconsin statute does not itself require parent routing (the thread's assertion is unverified). Estimate of minors with SSNs is 2,800.
H. Indemnification/Lakeshore: BAA s.7.1 uncapped for negligence; root cause (unpatched CVE-2025-1847, patch 3/18, 14-day SLA missed, Nov 2024 Item #7) makes negligence defensible only weakly; note SLA inconsistency: Forensic Report cites a 14-day SLA (IT-POL-2023-009), Risk Assessment cites a 30-day stated SLA and 45-60 day actual cycle. BAA s.4.4: credit monitoring >=12 months at BA expense; s.4.4(c) reimburse notice costs. Reply to Lakeshore by May 19 (they demand by May 21): cooperate, no admissions; AG notice for Illinois is the CE's/agent's task, confirm via written delegation. Lakeshore's ask whether Illinois AG has been notified: not yet.
I. Insurance: Policy NM-CL-2024-08812 is claims-made-and-reported, period ends June 30, 2025: report Lakeshore's demand and BAA claims as circumstances before expiry. Consent required before assuming client costs (s.5.2; $50,000 emergency cap); Apex and Sentinel need insurer approval; BAA indemnity likely uninsured (contract exclusion). Credit monitoring 61,200 x $12 x 24 = $17,625,600 alone exceeds the $10M limit; total estimated breach cost $19.0M-$24.0M vs $10.25M SIR+limit: uninsured $9.25M-$13.75M. Consider offering shorter or opt-in monitoring (statutory minimums vary) and negotiating pricing. Policy 'discovery' definition differs from HIPAA; notice May 3 timely.
J. Document inconsistencies: forensic firm name (Oakvale Point vs 'Bridgepoint' in filename/signature/report number; investigator Traherne vs 'Trahan'); spreadsheet also labels source as Oakvale; Bayview CA/OR split 5,900/2,800 (spreadsheet) vs 5,500/3,200 (Timeline); 42 affected clients vs 347; 35 vs 7 telehealth; memo due May 21 (email) vs May 22 (Timeline); Risk Assessment Q2 2025 target had not yet lapsed; Texas deadline column header; Policy cites 164.402(2)(iv) for the safe harbor (the safe harbor is HHS guidance under the 'unsecured PHI' definition).
K. Privilege: forensic report is 'DRAFT' and distribution-limited; avoid sharing with insurer/clients beyond need (Report App. C); consider final report separation (business vs legal); communications with vendors and the carrier risk waiver.
L. Next steps: (1) written discovery determination and Policy amendment; (2) notify all BAA clients and 35 telehealth clients by May 30 with installment plan; (3) obtain CE authorizations (BAA s.4.5) and insurer consent; (4) verify State chart against primary statutes; (5) HHS portal filings and media releases timed with mailings; (6) vendor contracts (Apex, Sentinel) after consent; (7) report to carrier before June 30; (8) execute BAAs with telehealth clients; (9) preserve evidence.
